sources.note: Shows that the roughly 20% of CoT tokens with the highest entropy act as decision forks, and that restricting RLVR policy-gradient updates to only those tokens matches or beats full-gradient training, with the advantage growing with model size.
sources.title: Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning

sources.note: Shows that greedy decoding is not deterministic across hardware: changing GPU type, GPU count or evaluation batch size shifts a reasoning model's AIME'24 accuracy by up to 9 percentage points and its response length by 9,000 tokens under BF16, because floating-point addition is non-associative.
sources.title: Understanding and Mitigating Numerical Sources of Nondeterminism in LLM Inference

result.definition: The 32B member of the Qwen3 family. It appears in these sources as a scale check rather than a primary subject — used to verify that numerical-precision reproducibility findings established at 7-8B also hold at larger scale, and as a large model in entropy-mechanism experiments. Results for it are generally deferred to appendices in the sources that use it. Note that this entry is filed as a dataset because the archived summaries listed evaluated models in the dataset field; it is a model, not a corpus.
